full_judgment:
2. The material facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, is that the predecessor of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-11 Abdul Karim instituted Title Suit No.137 of 1976 in the Court of learned Munsif, 3rd Court, Sadar, Jessore against the defendants for declaration of title and confirmation of possession over the suit land. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to one Ayezuddin Biswas and during his possession he settled the suit land to Abdul Karim, the predecessor of the plaintiff-opposite parties by way of registered Kabuliyat dated 05.3.1937. The "Kha" schedule land belonged to Chandra Bibi and she settled the suit land to Abdul Karim by way of Kabuliyat dated 24.6.1950 at a rental of Rs.5/5/- Annas. Since the date of settlement the plaintiffs had been owning and possessing the suit land. But -/8/- Annas share of the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants which is wrong and fraudulent. The defendants have got no right, title and interest and possession in the suit land. The cause of action to file the suit arose on 27th of Chaitra, 1387 B.S. when the defendants denied the plaintiff's title and threaten to dispossess from the suit land. Hence, the plaintiff was compelled to file the instant suit. 

 3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. The defendant's case, in short, is that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to Herajatullah and Derajatullah under the landlord of Motinessa and others and the "Kha" schedule land also belonged to Heraj and Deraj in equal share under the landlord Roton Bibi and during their possession C.S. record of rights correctly published their name. Deraj died leaving his daughter Hajari and brother Heraj. Heraj died leaving two sons namely Abdul Karim, the deceased plaintiff and Abdul Jalil, the predecessor of the defendants. The share of Heraj was devolved upon both Abdul Karim and Abdul Jalil equally. Abdul Karim instituted the suit. Thereafter, Abdul Karim died leaving one widow, 5 sons and 5 daughters and Abdul Jalil died leaving this defendants. This contesting defendants inherited -/8/-Annas share in the suit land through their father. The -/8/- Annas share of the suit land has rightly been recorded in the name of this defendants. The defendants have been owning and possessing their share land. The father of the plaintiff never acquired the suit land alone. The plaintiff did not possess -/16/- Annas share, rather they possess their -/8/- Annas share in the suit land. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 5. At the trial both the parties led their respective evidence to prove their case. The plaintiff examined as many as 4 P.Ws. and the defendants also examined 4 D.Ws. The trial Court after considering the materials on record dismissed the suit. 

 8. Mr. M.A. Wahab, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Court of appeal below committed an error of law apparent on the face of the records by observing that "it cannot be concluded that the title and interest of the land remained with the recorded persons simply because the land was recorded in their names at the time of C.S. operation" which is a clear violation of the provision of Section 103 B(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act. He further added that the appellate Court below committed an error of law in holding that "the Kabuliyat Ext.2 and 2(a) sufficiently proved that Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule lands respectively" in view of the fact that there is no iota of evidence either in the plaint or in the deposition of the witnesses of the plaintiffs that Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi ever acquired the disputed land from the admitted recorded tenants Derajtullah Biswas and Herajtulalh Biswas rather it is on the record that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to Satkori Mitra and Hemlal Mitra which is all together a wrong,false and baseless in view of the Exts.3(d) and 3(e). He further submitted that the Court of appeal below committee an error of law by giving importance and reliance upon the Kabuliyat Exts.2 and 2(a) which have not been legally and properly proved by the plaintiff in this case. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law in holding that "Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the land of C.S Khatian No.47 and C.S Khatian No.207," in fact that there is no evidence to that effect that both of them took settlement of the said "Ka" and "Kha" schedule lands respectively from the original owner. He added that the appellate Court also committed an error of law in placing reliance upon the S.A. record in respect of the non-disputed land. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law by misreading the deposition of witnesses, particularly the deposition of the D.Ws. 2 and 3. He further submitted that the appellate Court also committed an error of law in not considering the evidence of P.W.1 Abdus Salam who has admitted the possession of the defendant No.1 in the disputed Plot Nos.50 and 52 by deposing that the distance between the homestead of the plaintiffs and the defendants No.1 Soleman is one bighat only, where in the defendant No.1 has admittedly been resided with his family in his ancestral homestead situated in the same Plot. In such view of the evidence the appellate Court erred in law in not holding that the defendants are in possession of the suit land. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law in placing importance and relying upon the Dhakilas Ext.1-series which have not been proved in accordance with law and the procedure. He further submitted that Ext.1 series are not genuine, rather forged, fraudulent and created for the purpose of the suit. But the appellate Court below committed an error of law on relying upon the Dhakilas Ext.1- series and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He also submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law. in not considering the petition filed by the respondent No.1 stating that the respondent No.2 died on 7.10.1980 and the appeal was abated as the heir/heirs of respondent No.2 Chandra Bibi was not made party in time. He added that the plaintiffs must prove his own case and weaknesses of the defence case, the plaintiff will not be entitled to get any benefit. According to him the' plaintiff failed to prove the case resulting which the trial Court dismissed the suit. But the appellate Court below without controverting the findings of the trial Court on misreading the evidence, misconstrued the documents, thus, mere surmise and conjecture allowed the appeal. He also referred the evidence of D.Ws. and submitted that from which it is apparent that the appellate court committed error of law, and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Having gone though the impugned judgment it appears that the appellate Court opined "that the plaintiffs have produced certified copy of the Kabuliyat dated 05.2.1937 Ext.2 and the certified copy of the Kabuliyat dated 24.6.1950 Ext.2(a) to show that Ayejudiin Biswas acquired C.S. Plot Nos.50 and 52 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.47 and Chandra Bibi became owner of the entire land of C.S. Khatian No.207. The Kabuliyat Ext.2 was executed about 45 years back and Kabuliyat Ext.2(a) was executed more than 30 years back, so in my opinion that those old documents should be given due importance. It has been argued on behalf of the defendant-respondent that the plaintiff could not produce any document to show as to how Ayejudiin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired their interest in the suit Plots. It is true that the plaintiffs have not produced any documents regarding the title of Ayejuddin Biswas in "Ka" schedule land and Chandra Bibi in respect of "Kha" schedule land. I think the Kabuliyat Ext.2 and 2(a) sufficiently proved that Ayejuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule land respectively. If Ayejuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi had no interest in the said property, there was no reason why Abdul Karim (since dead) would execute Kabuliyat in their favour." After appreciating the materials on record I am of the view that the above findings neither correct nor based on material evidence on record. Further this court is of the view that while C.S. record of rights admittedly stands in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants by executing Kabuliyat one of them i.e. by plaintiff, surely no right, title will create by such Kabuliyat either in favour of Kabuliyat giver and receiver. Kabuliyat receiver, or giver must proved that he had right, title and interest over suit property. In the instant case although Kabuliyat receiver was examined by the plaintiff as P.W. but he failed to produce any documentary evidence in his favour showing that he was the real owner of the suit khatian by any documentary evidence in other capacity, and as such, far away to admit the alleged Kabuliyat as his title. I am of the view that a unilateral Kabuliyat does not confer the title either parties without basis of proof of any documentary evidence. 

 12. On the other hand from the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial court opined that the defendant claimed ejmali possession and he claimed his title on the basis of heir of C.S. recorded tenant Herajtullah. Both the C.S. and S.A. porcha go to protect the right and title of defendant. It is the case of the defendant that the Kabuliyat, i.e., Exts.2 and 2(a) have been created for the purpose of case and those are forged and concocted documents. The appellate Court did not consider the legal aspect of the Exts.2 and 2(a) because according to the trial Court these 2 exhibits neither proved the title of the receiver and giver nor produced and proved in accordance with law. In my opinion Exts.2 and 2(a) since produced by the plaintiff it is the onus of the plaintiff to prove the same in accordance with law but in the trial Court they have failed to prove these exhibits complying with the relevant provision of law. Moreover, one of the admitted owner if make any Kabuliyat in favour of title less third party admitting right, title and interest who has no such right and title, that unilateral Kabuliyat should not be admitted and accepted as title deed. Furthermore, on perusal of the material on record it appears that all the exhibits produced by the plaintiff received back by the plaintiff-opposite parties, although from this Court once again reminders were issued to produce the wanting exhibit documents before this Court but they failed to do so. Therefore, this court has no scope, chance or occasion to perused and consider the same. 

 13. The trial Court while dismissed the suit clearly opined that P.W3 claimed to be the son of Chandra Bibi and he deposes that his mother got the suit land by way of auction purchase, but no such paper has been connected or submitted before the any Courts. The trial Court also found that both in C.S. and S.A. Porcha of the suit land were not recorded in the name of Chandra Bibi. Only in S.A. Porcha of Khatian No.269 her name was included in equal share with the name of the father of the plaintiff and defendants. 

 14. From the depositions of the P.Ws and D.Ws and documentary evidence it clearly proved that father of the defendant was in possession of the suit property at the time of S.A. operation and since then the defendants had been owning and possessing the suit property which apparently admitted by the P.W1 in cross-examination. However, the court of appeal below failed to discuss the evidence in respect of C.S and S.A. record to its legal and true perspective which are the vital and most important documentary evidence in favour of not only defendant but also the plaintiff predecessor. So, it can not be said that the plaintiffs had and the defendant had no title over the suit land. 

 Apart from those documentary evidence it is further crystal clear from the oral and documentary evidence of the P,Ws that the Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi had no documentary evidence on which basis the title of late Abdul Karim can be conferred in his favour. On the other hand according to the provisions of section 103 B of the Bengal Tenancy. Act, 1885 the record of rights published in the name of tenant shall be conclusive proof of such Publication from which it is proved beyond all reasonable doubts that predecessor of Late Abdul Karim and Late Abdul Jalil were the real owner of the suit Khatian as per C.S. record of rights which never became unworthy by any other documentary evidence. In support of the above view I may profitably refer to the case of Akrab Ali and others Vs. Zahiruddin Kari and others reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81 wherein it was held: 

 "According to section 103(B)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect." 

 15. On the above facts, circumstances of the case and discussions made hereinabove I am of the firm view that the learned Additional District Judge did not correctly appreciate and construe the documents and materials on record in accordance with law in reversing the judgment of the trial Court. Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Jessore suffers from legal infirmity and perversity, and as such, the same is liable to be set aside. 

 19. Send down the lower Court record communicate this judgment at once.

2. The facts, in short, are that the plain-tiff respondents filed Title Suit No. 175 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Jhenaidha praying for declaration of their title and confirmation of possession and alleging dispossession from the suit property. During pendency of the suit a further prayer was made by amendment of the plaint for recovery of possession. The case of the plaintiff respondents was that the suit lands belonged to their predecessor in interest Amir Ali who died leaving the plaintiffs as his heirs and they were in possession of the suit lands and the defendants denied their title on the plea of settlement taken by Mojibur Rahman predecessor of the aforesaid defendants and that the defendants wrongly prepared the record of rights in their names. The defendant Nos. 1, 2, 4 and 5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter, alia, that Amir Ali took loan when he was on his death bed from Mojibur Rahman, predecessor of the defendants and agreed to make settlement of the property in exchange and that Amir Ali gave direction to his heirs, the present plaintiffs who were minors at that time except Mujibunnessa and Dilzan Nessa, the two wives of Amir Ali, to execute necessary document in favour of Mojibur Rahman. The heirs of Amir Ali accordingly made settlement of the suit land in favour of Mojibur Rahman. In pursuance of the settlement Mojibur Rahman executed three kabuliyats in favour of the plaintiffs who granted rent receipts on realization of rents. The S. A record of right was prepared in the names of the defendants who are in possession of the suit land. 

 8. We have considered the submissions made at the Bar and perused the materials on record. It appears that both the parties admitted Amir Ali predecessor of the plaintiff respondents to be the original owner of the suit property. That being the position the plaintiffs claim merits consideration unless their claim is dislodged by any satisfactory evidence to the contrary. In denial of the claim of the plaintiff respondents, evidence has been adduced on behalf of the defendant appellants. The evidence includes oral and documentary. 

 9. It has been emphasized on behalf of the defendant respondents that record of rights standing in their names and subsequent payment of rent exclude the possibility of existence of any right or title of the plaintiff respondents. Mr. khan referring to such contention submits that on the cloak of valueless kabuliyats the defendants misleading the survey staff got their names recorded in the record of rights and based on such wrong record of rights, the defendants obtained rent receipts showing payment of rent. In view of the facts and circumstances and materials on record this contention of the learned Counsel for the plaintiff respondents cannot be brushed aside

lawyer:
Qumrul Hoque Siddique, Advocate instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellants.

Imam Sirajul Hoque and another -------- Appellants
VS
Director General, Land Record and Survey, Tejgaon, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. In the writ petition it was contended, inter-alia, that the name of the appellants recorded correctly in respect of disputed land situated under Bogura Settlement Zone. Against such record-of-rights some persons raised objection under rule 30 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, which was ultimately rejected. Thereafter Appeal Case Nos.1810/95, 1811/95, 1813/95, 1812/95, 1814/95 and 1889/95 under rule 31 of the said Rules were dismissed by the Appellate Authority by an order dated 24-8-2000 on the ground of limitation. Eventually, one Rokyea Begum filed an application before the Ministry of Land and on the basis of the said application writ-respondent No.2, Director of Lands after making an inquiry set-aside the earlier order of dismissal of the appeals without serving any notice to the appellants and appointed respondent No.3, Assistant Settlement officer for re-hearing of the appeals. Consequently, the proceedings of all of the 5 (five) appeals were again started. The appellants without finding any other alternative remedy compelled to file the Writ Petition challenging the proceeding of said appeals. 

 4. The writ-respondent Nos.5 and 6 contested the writ petition by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition contending, inter-alia, that, the writ-petitioners-appellants filed an application for setting aside the order of restoration passed by the Director, Land Records before the Director General, Land Records and Surveys on 7-10-2001 and without waiting for the result of the said application filed the Writ Petition on 15-10-2001 which is not maintainable and is liable to be discharged. They further contended that the Director of land Records in exercising the power conferred upon him as per provision of Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 restored the appeal cases. It was further contended that, the Director, Land Records in due exercise of his power set-aside the dismissal order of the appeals and passed a legal and valid order for re-hearing of the appeals by a competent Assistant Settlement Officer under Bogura Zonal settlement Office and hence, there is no illegality in passing the order of restoration. It was further contended that, at the time of attestation, the attestation officer on the basis of a false and fabricated deed of gift dated 16-6-1942 deleted the names of some heirs, who raised objection under Rule 30 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and the objection officer illegally rejected the same and against the said rejection order they filed the appeals within date but the Authority has been wrongly dismissed the appeals solely on ground of limitation on 21-8-2000. Against the order of dismissal the writ-respondent No.5 filed an application before the Ministry of Land who forwarded the said application to the Director General, Land Records and Surveys. The Director General, Land Records and Surveys ordered Director, Land Records to take necessary action for disposal of the matter. The Director, Land Records ordered the Zonal Settlement Officer, Bogura for disposal of the appeals after re-hearing the same as because the appeals were filed within the limitation period. But the writ-respondent No-5 filed an application before the Director, Land Records to the effect that they would not get justice at Bogura Settlement Office and hence on 3-9-2001 the said officer passed an order to settle the appeals by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Zonal Settlement Office, Dhaka. 

 8. Mr Hoque further submits that in the instant case no allegation of fraud has been proved, thus the order passed by the Director of Land Records is absolutely illegal and without lawful authority and the High Court Division in passing the impugned order failed to consider this legal aspect and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside. 

 9. Mr Hoque also submits that Director of Land Records and Surveys having been upgraded to Director General of Land Records and the Director of Land Records being a sub-ordinate officer, the exercise of power under Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 by the said Director of Land Records is illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 10. Per contra, Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the respondent Nos.5(a)-(d) and 6 submits that the High Court Division correctly held that the Director of land Records and the Director of Land Records and Survey is the same officer, when this officer performs his duty as regards the matter of land records only, he is designated as Director of Land Records, So, it is not acceptable at all that the Director of Land Records is not authorized to exercise the power of Rule 44 of Tenancy Rules. The correctness of the view taken by the High Court Division could be further clear from rule 44 which contemplates the powers of Revenue-Officers under Chapter XIV of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1955. 

 11. Mr Necigi further submits that a complaint made by Rokeya Begum [predecessor of respondents No. 5(a)-(d)] to the Ministry of Land would clearly show that deprivation of female heirs in the district of Bogura by some Revenue and Settlement Officers led by the then Zonal Settlement Officer has been categorically alleged with material particulars, and the Government in the Ministry of Land taking into consideration the entire perspectives and facts of the case directed the Directorate of Land Records and Surveys to look into the matter, who passed the order impugned in the writ petition. 

 12. Mr Neogi having referred to the memo No. ত্বঃ গরঃ ২৩/৯৫/খন্ড-১)১৬৬৬ তারিখ ২৩-৮-২০০১ issued by the Director, Land Records addressed to the zonal settlement office, Bogura submits that on an inquiry it was found that fraud had committed in disposing the 05 appeals in question and thus, the competent authority cancelled the orders and directed the competent settlement officer to hear the appeals afresh. The above order was passed by the Director, Land Records within its jurisdiction and thus, the instant appeal is liable to dismissed. 

 142A. Correction of fraudulent entry before final publication of record-of-rights—The Revenue-officer, with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' shall, on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquiries as he deems necessary, direct excision of the fraudulent entry and his act in doing so shall not be open to appeal. At the same time, the Revenue-officer shall make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his finding in a formal proceeding for the purpose of future reference. 

 "After final publication of the record-of-right, after the SA Survey the only mode tor correction of the same was through it Court and thus subsequent to preparation of SA record-of-right, the RS record-of-right was prepared and after final publication thereof the mode for correction of any wrong entry appearing in the RS record was through Civil Court and without moving the Civil Court no correction in recent records of right is lawful or permissible and, as such, the draft record-of-right in the instant case having been prepared following the preparation of the SA and RS records in accordance with law, the attempts of the leave petitioner for correction under Rules 30 and 31 of the State Acquisition Rules,1955 have failed. The plain reading of the application dated 14-7-2002 allegedly filed under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955, ex-facie appears to be a vague application, inasmuch as the said post contains no specific allegation of any act of fraud and it is the settled principle of law that an application, not having disclosed any act of fraud in its body, is not entertainable and  liable to be rejected." 

 "From the order of the Director General, it appears that there was no  finding or observation of the Director General that the writ-petitioner-respondents managed to procure the entry  in the record-of-right by practicing fraud or entry was fraudulent one or that he  consulted the relevant records or that made  other enquires or that gave the parties  concerned a hearing concerned a hearing in  as much as Rule 42A of the Rules  empowered the Director General to correct  the entry after due compliance of the aforesaid legal requirements. Rule 42 provided that a Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of a "Settlement Officer" may, at any time before the publication of final record-of-rights, direct that any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28 to 32 in respect of a district, or local area, should be cancelled and that the proceedings should be taken up fresh from such stage as he may direct. But in the instant proceeding, as it appears from the order of the Director General, that the provisions of Rule 42A and 42 had not been followed, that is, it is apparent from the order of the Director General itself that the same was unlawful." 

 17. In view of the above settled proposition it is clear that a Revenue-officer, with the additional designating of 'settlement officer' has got the authority/jurisdiction to re-open an appeal if on receipt of an application or on receipt of official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquires as he deems necessary, direct excision of fraudulent entry and at the same time, revenue officer has got the power to make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his findings. 

 18. Thus, it is crystal clear that if fraud has been done in recording of right before final publication thereof, the Revenue Officer can hear the matter afresh after consulting relevant records, making such other enquiry necessary, if he deems and giving opportunity of being heard of the parties. 

 20. Mr Hoque has raised another issue that Director of Land Records has no authority to pass an order pursuant to the Rule 44 of Rules, 1955 as the said post has been upgraded as Director General of Land Records and Surveys. 

 "44. Powers vested in Director of Land Records and Surveys:—In respect of all operations under Chapter XVII of the Act which have been placed under the administrative control of the Director of Land Records and Surveys, Bangladesh, he may discharge all the functions of a Revenue-Officer under the said Chapter and shall have all the powers of a Settlement Officer under rules 36, 38,39, 40, 41, 42, 42A and 42B." 

 22. Upon perusal of the above rule it is clear that the Director of Land Records and Surveys has been vested with the power to discharge all functions of a Revenue Officer and shall have all powers of Settlement Officer under rule 42A along with some other rules in respect of all operation under chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 23. In the instant case it reveals from the record that predecessors of the present Respondents No.5(a)-(d), Rokeya Begum, filed a compliant before the Ministry of Land regarding the alleged fraudulent entry in the record and thereafter Ministry of Land forwarded the same to Director General, Land Records and Surveys who ordered the Director, Land Records to dispose of the matter. Thereafter Director, Land Records after making an enquiry on the allegation made by Rokeya Begum and upon consideration of the said enquiry report he set-aside the orders passed in 05 appeals and directed a competent officer to hold hearing of the appeals in question. 

 24. The letter dated 23-8-2001 contains the decision of Director, Land Records runs as follows: 

 25. From the above, it is clear that fraudulent act had been committed in disposal of the appeal Nos.1810/95, 1811/95, 1813/95, 1812/95, 1814/95 and 1889/95 under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and concerned authority i.e. Director Land Records after holding enquiry passed the necessary orders, which is within the ambit of rule 42A and 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 26. From ‘ভূমি রেকর্ড ও জরিপ অধিদপ্তর কর্মকর্তাদের দায়িত্ব’ as produced before this court by Mr Hogue, it transpires that Director-General of Land Records and Surveys Directorate has been empowered to ‘অধীনস্থ কর্মকর্তাদেরকে প্রয়োজনীয় ক্ষমতা অর্পণের আদেশ প্রদান।’ And Director, Land. Records is bound to do perform any assignment delegated to him by the Director-General. Thus, in exercising power under rule 42A and 44, the Director, Land Records did not commit any illegality; rather he passed the same within his jurisdiction. Thus, we find no substance in the submission of Mr Hoque, that the Director, Land Records had passed the order exceeding his jurisdiction.

full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that Shafiuddin and another instituted aforesaid suit for declaration of their title and recovery of khas possession stating that the land as described in the schedule to the plaint belonged to Maizuddin who died leaving behind one son, Plaintiff No.1 and widow the plaintiff No.2 as his heirs. The plaintiffs, constructing dwelling homestead in 0.17 acre of land of plot No.187, had been residing therein. The defendants forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs on 25-10-1985. The plaintiffs came to know that SA record of right in respect of the suit land was wrongly prepared in the names of the defendants. Hence, was the suit. 

 3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit contending that the landlords of the disputed joma were Nagendra Roy Mukhopadhya and others and tenant was Maizuddin. Maizuddin defaulted to pay the rent. Thus, the landlords, instituting a Rent Suit, got decree and took over the said property in his possession executing the said decree. Thereafter, Baser Mollah, predecessor-in-interest of the defendant, took settlement of the said land from the landlords and took over possession of the same. SA record was prepared in the name of the plaintiff No.1. Accordingly, the defendant filed objection case which was allowed. This defendant has been possessing the suit land for more than 12 years. The suit should be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court, on consideration of the evidence on record, dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs preferred appeal, which was allowed by the appellate Court. 

 6. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellants, submits that the plaintiffs are the successive heirs of CS recorded tenants and they were in possession of the suit land till the date of dispossession on 25-10-1985 and the plaintiffs, by adducing sufficient evidences, proved their title and possession and, thereafter, date of dispossession. He submits that the last Court of facts upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record, found plaintiffs' title, possession and their dispossession in the suit land, the High court Division erred in law in setting aside the well reasoned judgment of the appellate Court. He further submits that the defendants claimed that the suit land was sold in auction and the landlords auction purchased the same and took over the possession of the same, thereafter settled the suit land to the predecessor-in-interest of the contesting defendants but they hopelessly failed to prove the story of alleged auction and their allegedly settlement, the High Court Division upon improper consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties erroneously dismissed the suit. 

 7. Mr Garib Newaz, learned Advocate appearing for the respondents, submits that it is the duty of the plaintiffs to prove their own case to get the decree and their possession in the suit land till the date of dispossession, the High Court Division upon proper appreciation of the materials on record, rightly reversed the judgment and decree of the appellate Court. He further submits since the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession till the date of their dispossession, the trial Court as well as the revisional Court upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record, came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs suit was barred by limitation. 

 8. Admittedly, Moizuddin was CS recorded tenant. The plaintiffs' case is that they are the successive heirs of the said Moizuddin and had been possessing the suit land till the date of their dispossession dated 25-10-1985. At the initial stage, SA record-of-rights was prepared in their names but finally it was published in the name of contesting defendants. It was their case that the plaintiff No.1 who is PW 1 was minor at the time of preparation of record-of-rights and the contesting defendant was his close relative and after the death of his father, they started to live in the house of the defendants. Taking opportunity of his minority, the defendant forcedly dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land. 

 9. It appears from the materials on record that earlier before the publication of SA operation, a Miscellaneous Case for correction of record-of-rights was filed which was disposed of on contest. Finally SA record-of-rights was prepared and published in the name of defendant No.1. On perusal of the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the Trial Court considered the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the parties and came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession till their alleged date of dispossession from the suit land. It further held that the suit was barred by limitation. While drawing conclusion as to the possession of the plaintiffs till their dispossession, the first Court of fact considered the evidence adduced by the parties vividly but from the judgment and decree of the appellate Court it appears that the appellate Court, without taking into consideration of the evidence as quoted by the trial Court, abruptly reversed the finding as to the possession of the plaintiffs till their dispossession from the suit land. The revisional Court reversed the finding as to the possession and dispossession arrived at the appellate Court holding that the conclusion arrived at by the last Court of fact is not based on evidence. In the plaint, the plaintiffs stated that they were dispossessed by the defendant on 25-10-1985 from the suit land, plaintiff No.1 was examined as PW 1 who in his evidence did not utter a word about the alleged date of dispossession. Similarly their another witness PW 2 has also said nothing about the date of dispossession of the plaintiffs from the same. We have also gone through the judgment of the Courts below it appears to us that the conclusion arrived at by the High Court Division is correct.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 231 of 2010
lawyer:
Goutam Kumar Roy, Deputy Attorney General instructed by Md. Shamsul Alam, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
N.K. Saha, Senior Advocate instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Dhaka and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Bimal Saha alias Jhantu Saha and other ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein as petitioners (hereinafter referred to as the writ-petitioners) filed the writ petition before the High Court Division for a Rule Nisi calling upon writ-respondent Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why should not be directed to perform their public duties by incorporating the names of the writ-petitioners in the record-of-rights by way of mutation in R.D. Khatin No. 55 of Mouza Shamair under Police Station-Saver, District-Dhaka in respect of the property described in detail in paragraph No. 5 of the writ petition and accordingly, the Rule Nisi was issued. 

 3. The case of the writ-petitioners is that they are the sons of Mohan Saha of village-Birulia, under Police Station- Savar, District- Dhaka. During preparation of the record-of-rights under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the landed property measuring an area 9.59 acres of Mouza Shamiar, under Police Station-Savar, District- Dhaka was recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 15 and S.A. Plot No. 67 (hereinafter referred to as the landed property) in equal share in the names of Gopi Ballav Saha and Nan Ballav Saha. The landed property appertained to C.S. Khatian No. 4. Thereafter the landed property was recorded in R.S. Plot Nos. 176 and 177 in R.S. Khatian No. 55 of Mouza Shamair in the name of said Gopi Ballav Saha in equal share. Gopi Ballav Saha died leaving behind the writ-petitioners as two sons who inherited the entire 9.59 acres of the landed property. The writ-petitioners by a registered power of attorney dated the 31st day of January, 2004 appointed Alhaj Md. Abdul Hai, son of late Haji Amir Chan Bepari of No. 24 Katasur, Police Station- Mohammadpur, District-Dhaka as their attorney in order to do all acts in civil, criminal and revenue Courts as well as in all other statutory bodies for protection and well management of the landed property. The attorney of the writ-petitioners applied to writ-respondent No. 3, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka for mutation of their names in the relevant record-of-rights. On the said application; writ-respondent No. 4, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Savar Upazila by Memo No. জেঃ প্রঃ ঢাঃ/ বাঃ বিবিধ সা-২/২০০৩-৭৪০ (নং) dated the 10th day of May, 2004 called for a report through writ-respondent No. 5, the Kanongo and accordingly, the Kanongo submitted a report on the 12th day of July, 2004 stating that S.A. recorded tenant - Gopi Ballav Saha had left the country during India-Pakistan war and as a result, 4.80 acres of land of S.A. Khatian No. 15 in his share was recorded as vested property in V.P. Case No. 338/75, the said 4.80 acres of land was leased out to Akub Ali, Suruj Ali, Joynal Abedin and Kuri Fakir. The said 4.80 acres of land has been enlisted at serial No. 966 under Vested Property Return Act, 2000. During the R.S. operation, S.A. Plot No. 67 was split up in two R.S. Plots being Nos. 176 and 177 covering 9.31 acres and .28 acre respectively and the same were recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 55 in he names of Gopi Ballav Saha and Pran Ballav Saha. During the R.S. operation, the landed property was not recorded as vested property. On the 13th day of July, 2004, writ-respondent No. 4 transmitted the report to writ-respondent No. 3 for necessary action. Despite receiving the aforesaid report of the Kanongo, writ-respondent No. 4 did not pass any order in the matter and hence the writ-petitioners filed V.P. Appeal No. 215/2004 before writ-respondent No. 6, the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka who by his order dated the 31st day of July, 2004 declared the entire proceedings including the order passed in V.P. Lease Case Nos. 235 of 76 and 338/75 illegal and void and directed writ-respondent No.4 to allow the proposed mutation subject to approval of writ-respondent No.1, the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and he sent the record of V.P. Appeal No. 215 of 2004 to writ-respondent No. 1 for approval. Thereafter, writ-respondent No. 1 on perusing the aforesaid order and the documents on record vide Memo No. ভূঃ মঃ/ শঃ-৬/অর্পিত/ঢাকা/১৫২/২০০৪/৩৮৮ dated the 19th day of May, 2005 asked writ-respondent No. 2, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to inform whether action was taken pursuant to the order of the Additional Divisional Commissioner or the aggrieved party filed any appeal against the same. Having noticed the reluctance of writ-respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 in taking necessary action for the proposed mutation, the writ-petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 351/2006 before writ-respondent No. 7, the Chairman, Land Appeal Board, Dhaka stating all the aforesaid facts upon which he passed an order on the 13th day of July, 2006 directing writ-respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 to take necessary action in the light of the letter dated the 19th day of May, 2005 of writ respondent No. 1 Even after receiving the aforesaid order of writ-respondent No. 7, writ-respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 kept silent and reluctant as before. In the circumstances, the writ-petitioners again filed an application before writ-respondent No. 6, the Additional Divisional Commissioner; Dhaka in V.P. Appeal No. 215/2004 for compliance with the order passed by the Land Appeal Board, the Secretary Ministry of Land as well as the order dated the 31st day of July, 2004 passed by him. In the said V.P. Appeal No. 215 of 2004, writ-respondent No. 6 by his order dated the 15th day of February, 2007, directed writ-respondent No. 4, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for mutation of the names of the writ-petitioners in the record-of-rights. 

 4. On receipt of aforesaid order dated the 15th day of February, 2007, writ-respondent No. 4 vide his Memo No. উভূঅ/সাভার/০৭-৬২৯/১(৬) dated the 6th day of March, 2007 directed writ-respondent No. 5, the Assistant Land Officer, Begunbari Union Land Office for mutating the names of the writ-petitioners by opening separate jots and to collect development tax in compliance with the order passed by the higher authorities. Thereafter writ-respondent No. 5 without allowing the proposed mutation by his Memo No. (কঃভূঃসঃ/২০০৭/১২) dated the 3rd day of September, 2007 informed writ-respondent No. 4 that after inspecting the records of his office and the documents submitted, he would inform as to what action would be taken but to the knowledge of the writ-petitioners till filing of the writ petition, writ-respondent No. 5 did not take any action. In the circumstances, on 18.06.2008, the writ-petitioners gave demand justice notice to writ-respondent Nos. 1-5 requesting them to allow the proposed mutation and report compliance thereof by the 26th day of June, 2008, but they refused to comply with the request; hence the writ petition. 

 5. It appears that no affidavit-in-opposition was filed by the writ-respondent Nos. 1-5 controverting the statements made in 41 the writ petition. And the learned Deputy Attorney General who appeared on behalf of the writ-respondents at the time of hearing the writ petition, in fact supported the case of the writ-petitioners as apparent from the impugned judgment. In the impugned judgment, it has been recorded that "The learned Deputy Attorney General entered appearance and candidly submits that there is no plausible reason for non-compliance with the order and that the respondent from the very beginning did not comply with the positive direction given on various occasion by the Government including the Chairman, Land Appeal Board for mutating the names of the petitioners. "The High Court Division on consideration of the writ petition and the annexures annexed thereto by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule Nisi absolute with the findings and the observations as under: 

 "It is apparent from the very statement in the petition by the petitioners that the petitioner with due diligence approached the respondents and took steps for mutation of the property in question. From Annexure-F to the petition it appears that on 13th July 2004 respondent No. 4, after accepting the report of the Kariongo directed for correction of records of right and for mutation and to take necessary steps accordingly. Thereafter on 31st July 2007 respondent No. 6 Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka directed that the names of the petitioners to be mutated by the Assistant Commissioner Land respondent No. 4 (Annexure-G) and pursuant to that order Assistant Secretary (respondent No. 4) vide his order dated 19th May 2005 asked the concerned authority to inform as to whether any action was taken pursuant to the judgment or filed and appeal against the judgment dated 30th November 2004 by the respondent No. 6 or that the order has been acted upon (Annexure-II).
