full_judgment:
2. In original plaint. it is stated that, suit land originally belonged to Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa Bibi Waif Estate, who made Waqf of the property by Waqf deed No. 30 dated 23.04.1864 and deed No. 373 dated 04.02.1877. Ahsanullah Khan Bahadur was one of the Mutwalli of this Waqf Estate and in cronological way, the members of the Nawab Family became Mutwalli and last Mutwalli was Nawab Khawja Hassan Askari, who was Mutwalli up to 1974. When cadastral survey started, this Waqf property as per deed and on the basis of Mutwalli, was included in the name of Nawab Courts of Wards represented by Nawab Sir Salimullah although as per record, it ought to be recorded in the name of Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa Bibi Waqf Estate. When Nawab Khawja Habibullah was Mutwalli, he, as per section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, by application dated 22.05.1934, enrolled the property as E.C. No. 411/C. Nawab Sir Salimullah while Mutwalli of Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa Bibi Waqf Estate, died leaving son, Nawab Khawja Habibullah. Nawab Khawja Habibullah died leaving son. Nawab Khawja Hasan Askari who continue as, Mutwalli till S.A. and R.S. survey started but due to mismanagement it was recorded in the name of lessee in S.A. and R.S. 

 khalian and due to the said wrong recording, huge quantity of Waqf property alienated. 

 (my registered deed did not get any fraction of land in the suit property. During S.A. survey the land was recorded in the name of defendant No.1 as the then Mutwalli was kept silent and defendant No.1 could not produce any paper in support of lease, recording was false. Plaintiff on 21.09.1988 filed application before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Dhaka for correction of S.A. khatian which has been recorded in Misc. Case No. 8/88. Additional Deputy 

 Commissioner (Rev) Dhaka advised the plaintiff to move before the Civil Court. The papers upon which defendant No. I and 2 claimed title are totally false and paper transaction and by that the property which has been dedicated to the “Allah” cannot alienated and right, title interest and possession of the Waif properly can not be extinguished as in the C.A. Roll the property has been recorded in the name of Mutwalli. After becoming Mutwalli of Waqf Estate, Alseruddin Hayder and Md. Mohiuddin Hayder, the Manager of the Estate wanted papers of the Estate from proforma defendant No.9 who told to collect papers front defendant Nos. 3-4 but plaintiff after making several takid to defendant Nos. 3-4 did not get original papers of the Estate. Defendant 

 well as in respect of title of the property of Waqf in favour of Waqf Estate. The suit was decreed against Nawab Sir Salimullah and others. Against which Nawab Sir Salimullah filed Appeal No. 389 of 1909 before the High Court Division at Calcutta and on contesting hearing the appeal was allowed on 30.08.1909 and in the judgment it is opined that Nawab Sir Salimullah for his live time would he the Mutwalli of Ainuddin Hayden and Faizunnessa Waqf Estate and plaintiff of that suit, Abul Khali Md. Mostfa or their heirs will never became the Mutwalli of the Estate. This Waqf Estate originally was for a vast property and the some of the land are managed by the Nawab Courts of Wards as C.S. khatian and C.A. roll recorded the name of Courts of Wards. Plaintiff filed case before the court of Settlement Dhaka under section 50 of the State Acquisition of Tenancy Act for correction and by order dated 27.04.1975 the C.A. roll recorded the name of Faizunnessa Bibi Waqf Estate but Mutwalliship was not corrected. Papers having not been collected earlier, the suit could not be filed earlier. Wagf Administrator in Memo -No. Ao: 0: Pro:/141 Dha: Da: dated 17.09.2001 gave permission to lessee Md. Kamrul Hasan for Netter interest of the Waqf Estate, for better interest of Ainuddin Hayder and Faizunnessa E.C. No. 41 11 C to continue the suit. On 27.05.1990 the Estate filed application to Mutwalli of Bangladesh Wag Administrator, Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for correction of record by Memo No. 698/Dhaka dated 07.06.1991) with written request to Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to cornea the record. Defendant Nos. I and 2 disclosed that they have purchased the suit land from defendant No. 3 to which plaintiff demanded purchase deed from defendant No.1 and 2 but they did not. As per paragraph No. 2 of the Waqf deed it has been slated that no lease can be sustainable for any period beyond 3 years: lease deed of defendant was for 3 years, as such defendant Nos. 3.4 has no right, title to settle the suit property. Particularly it has been further written in the plaint as:- 

 12. From the aforesaid statements made in the plaint it is crystal clear that the Waqf Estate had only superior interest in the land in suit as Jaminder, because the C.A. Roll prepared in the name of Jaminder for payment of compensation as per C.A. Roll. So the suit is barred by section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950. It is also found from the aforesaid statements of the plaint that the way estate had given alleged lease to the plaintiff the vacant and in lieu of yearly rents which is prohibited by section 26/A of the Nom Agricultural and Tenancy Act and also by section-75/A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 Since by dint of lease of the land no right is L created in favour of the lessee in the lease hold land the plaintiff, a tieless person cannot disturb or interfere with the ownership and possession of defendant No. 9 in the suit property, who acquired title through S.A. and R.S. recorded owner. 

 On the other hand, Mr. M. A. Rouf, appearing for the respondents argued that in deciding this point, the general scheme of the Act is to be taken into consideration. The general scheme of the Act is that for the purpose of taking over all interests that are liable to be acquired under the Act, preparation of record-of-rights is to be made and after final publication of the record-of-rights, assessment of compensation of the acquirable interests is to be made and finally published. It, however, seems that an exception has been made with regard to rent-receiving interests and special provisions for acquisition of the interests of certain rent-recovers have been made in Chapter II of Part 11 of the Act. According to the provisions of this Chapter, rent-receiving interests can be acquired by publication of Notification under section 3 of the Act even before the general provisions of the Act are given effect to, that is, before preparation of the record-of rights and preparation and publication of the Compensation Assessment roll. It may also be pointed out that according to the provisions of section 3 of the Act, before introduction of the sub-section (2a) M section 3 by way of amendment. Notification under section 3 was to be published with re3ference to particular estates, talks, tenures, holdings and tenancies and in respect of all rent-receivers whose properties were under the management of court of Wards Act, 1879. Sub-section (2a) was enacted and introduced in section 3 of the Act by Ordinance No.III of 1956. This provision namely, sub-section (2a) empowers the Government to publish Notification under section 3 in respect of rent-receivers by name or by reference to areas wherein they have interests or in such other manner as the Government might determine. It is after this amendment that general Notification dated 2nd April, 1956 were issued District-wise in regard to all rent-receiving interests which thereafter vested in the Government with effect from 14.4.56 in terms of those Notifications. So, Mr. Rout submitted that it was futile to argue that these interests. which were the subject-matter of the general Notifications, contained even after 14th April. 1956 and that they did not vest in the Government. His contention was that in the instant case the rent-receiving interests of the raiyat legally vested in the Government which became the proprietor by virtue of acquisition of the said interests. Accordingly from 14.4. 56 the Government alone became entitled, under the law, to receive the rent. The previous rent-receivers became divested of the right to receive rent and consequently they disappeared from the sense. On this point reference was made to subsection (4)(e) of section 3 which runs thus: 

 18. In the case of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and others-Vs-Resheda Begum and others, 14 MLR (AD) 401 it is held as: "Learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner, when confronted with the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 24.03.1952 and 29.02.1956, as to acquisition of rent receiving interest and the vesting of lands of the leave petitioners, including the case lands, found it difficult to substantiate the locustandi of the leave petitioner in challenging the draft records of right prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands prepared during the Mohanagar Survey. Further with the publication of the gazette notifications dated 24.03.1952 and 29.02.1956 the leave petitioner ceased to have any right, title and interest and possession in the case lands, because of acquisition. And vesting of said lands in the Government. The learned Additional Attorney General could not deny the granting of the ground rent payment receipts, copy of which have been annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition, admitting the writ petitioners as tenants under the Government. 

 On plaint reading of the Rule 42A, quoted above, it appears that the settlement officer is empowered to pass order only on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report, for correction of an entry in the record of right, procured by fraud, before final publication thereof. Thus the said Rule cannot be applicable in the instant case inasmuch as the record of right as prepared is in accordance with the past records of right prepared during S.A. Operation and R.S. Operation and there being no change as to the names as appearing in the said records of rights the question of fraud in recording the entry of names in the recent record of right prepared after the Mohanagar Survey does not arise. Apart from that after final publication of the record of right after the S.A. Survey the only - mode for correction of the same was through Civil Court and thus subsequent to preparation of S.A. record of right, the R.S. record of right was prepared and alter final publication thereof the mode for correction of any wrong entry appearing in the R.S. record was through Civil Court and without moving the Civil Court no correction in those records of right is lawful or permissible and as such the draft record of right in the instant case having been prepared following the preparation of the S.A. and R.S. records in accordance with law. the attempts of the leave petitioner for correction under Rules-30 and 31 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 have failed. The plaint reading of the application dated 14.07,2002, quoted above, allegedly tiled under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955. ex-facie appears to be a vague application inasmuch as the said application do not contain any specific allegation of any such of fraud and it is the settled principle of law that an application, not having disclosed any act of fraud it its body, is not entertaining and liable to be rejected. Without 'correcting the S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian as prepared in respect of the case lands in accordance with law earlier the leave petitioner cannot get its name entered in the recent record of right prepared during Mohanagar Survey allegedly only on the basis of C.S. Khatian." 

 (ii) All interests of all rent-receivers whose properties are, for the time being under the management of the Court of Words under the Court of Words Act. 1879, in their respective estates, taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies, as the case may be including all their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies. 

 25. Send down the lower court records.

caseno:
Civil Appeal No.35 of 2008
(Arising out of C.P.No.1438 of 2006)
lawyer:
Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants. 
Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiya, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Mohammad Ali Azam, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Kabir Ahmed being dead his heirs 1(a) Mahmuda Khatun being dead her heirs: Noor Mohammad and others ------ Appellants.
-Versus-
Mahohar Ali and others -------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs, in brief, is that the land of suit schedules 1 and 2 originally belonged to Abdul Hakim and Imam Uddin. The suit schedule 1 land was auction purchased by the Government in certificate case No.662 of 1936-37 for arrear of rent. Abdul Hakim and Imam Uddin surrendered the suit schedule 2 land in favour of Government due to their inability to pay rent of the same. Thereafter, the Government settled the suit schedule 1 and 2 land in favour of one Bazlul Karim in settlement case No.57 𝑜𝑓 1937−38 / 88 𝑜𝑓 1937−38 and the settled land was included in the family jote No.3. The homestead of said Bazlul Karim was situated at a distance of 30 miles from the suit land. The defendant No.1 on bringing money from Bazlul Karim paid rent to the government. Bazlul Karim sold the suit land to the plaintiffs by a kabala dated 22.01.1980 and made over possession thereof to them. On 20.03.1995 the defendant Nos.2-7 claimed title of the suit land by way of purchase disclosing that the M.R.R. and B.S. record of rights in respect of the suit land have been prepared in the name of their vendor Gura Miah the defendant No.1. The M.R.R and B.S. record of rights in respect of the suit land have been wrongly prepared in the name of the defendants, alleged vendor. The defendants did not acquire right and title by virtue of aforesaid wrong M.R.R. and B.S. Khatian. The plaintiffs asked the defendants to execute deed of relinquishment in respect of the suit land in their favour for several occasions but the defendants did not pay heed to the same and as such the plaintiffs were compelled to file the suit praying for reliefs stated above. 

 4. The defendant Nos.2-7 contested the suit denying material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. The suit is also barred under section 42 of the specific Relief Act. The suit land is in possession of the defendants and as such without prayer for consequential relief paying advalorem court fees, the suit as framed is not maintainable in law. The settlement of the suit land as stated by the plaintiffs was taken by Bazlul Karim with joint family fund and for the interest of the joint family Bazlul Karim settled the suit land with the defendant No.1 in 1952 by a dakhila and accordingly M.R.R. and B.S. record of rights were correctly prepared and finally published in the name of Gura Miah, defendant No.1. Gura Miah sold .40 acres of land from the land of suit schedule 2 in favour of the defendant Nos.2-7 and Abdur Sukkur by a kabala dated 08.02.1974 and accordingly made over possession thereof to them. Gura Miah sold the remaining .39 acres of land to Nazir Ahmed and Khatija by registered kabala dated 18.01.1974 who died leaving behind Manoara and others who sold the aforesaid .39 acres of land to the defendant Nos.5,7 and one Dilwara Begum by a kabala dated 09.11.1995. The plaintiffs did not implead Abdul Sukkur and Dilwara Begum as parties in the suit and as such the suit is bad for defect of parties. The plaintiffs had/have no right, interest and possession in the suit land and on the other hand the defendants have been in continuous, uninterrupted and peaceful possession of the suit land i.e. .79 acres of land on payment of rent since their purchase. The plaintiffs are not entitled to the relief as prayed for in the suit. 

 11. Per contra, Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiya, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for contesting defendants-respondents submits that the trial court in consideration of the evidence of PWs and DWs and of the fact of non-payment of rent by the plaintiffs or their predecessor, recording of MRR Khatian and BS Khatian in the name of the defendant’s vendor Gura Miah had arrived at the conclusion that the plaintiffs have no possession in the suit land and the appellate court not having reversed this finding with reference to the evidence considered by the trial court, the suit for simple declaration without prayer for recovery of khas possession is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. 

 12. Mr. Bhuiya further submits that Gura Miah claimed to have taken settlement of the suit land from Bazlul Karim and the suit land having been recorded in the MRR Khatian and B.S. Khatian in the name of Gura Miah who was in possession of the suit land and the suit land having been transferred by Gura Miah by registered deed dated 05.02.1974 and 18.01.1974 to the defendants the registered documents are not void but valid and are to be avoided by filing suit against the registered documents for declaration that the documents are invalid and not binding on the plaintiffs before claiming title in the land transferred by those documents and the same not having been done the suit is barred by law as found by the trial court and the same has not been rightly reversed by the appellate court and the High Court Division affirmed this finding of the trial court and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. 

 13. He also submits that the appellate court did not consider that P.W-2 being the brother of plaintiff No.2 and P.W-3 being the son-in-law of the plaintiff No.2 are not at all credible witnesses and the plaintiffs could not adduce any independent witness to support their claim of possession. The High Court Division on proper consideration of the materials on record came to a correct decision that plaintiffs are not entitled to get a decree as prayed for and that the defendants-respondents proved their title by exhibiting their relevant papers and documents. 

 14. We have considered the rival submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties, perused the impugned judgment as well as the judgments of the courts below and the evidence on record. 

 16. However, it appears from the record that eventually the plaintiffs filed an application under order 6 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint with a prayer to correct the prayer to the effect; 

 18. In the instant case the plaintiffs have sought declaration of title over the suit property and that the M.R.R. and B.S. record in respect of the suit property is wrong. 

 19. The trial Court as well as the High Court Division on scrutiny of the evidence on record held that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession in the suit land and hence suit is hit by proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 21. The trial court on proper consideration of the evidence on record held that the plaintiffs could not file a single dakhila to prove their possession over suit land; though, the plaintiffs claimed title on the strength of the deed dated 21.01.1980 exhibit-9, but no rent receipt was produced. The trial court also disbelieved the evidence of P.Ws-2 and 3 in regard to the evidence of possession as P.W-2 is the full brother and P.W-3 is the son-in-law (জামাই) of plaintiff No.2. The trial Court also held that Gura Miah was the possessor of the said suit land at the time of B.S. khatian, so B.S. khatian rightly record in the name of Gura Miah from where other defendants purchased the suit land vide various deeds, exhibit-kha, kha-1 and Ga and those deeds were not challenged by the plaintiffs and as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any relief under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The court of appeal below without adverting to the above findings of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit. 

 22. Having considered the evidence on record, we have no hesitation to agree with the findings of the trial court as well as the High Court Division that since the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession in the suit land, the present suit for declaration simpliciter without a prayer for consequential relief is hit by proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and as such the present suit is not maintainable.

caseno: Appeal From Original Decree No. 16 of 1988
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Abu Baker: For the plaintiff- appellants
Mr. Md. Shahidul Alam Chowdhury:  For defendant-respondent No. 2
parties:
Md. Amjad Hossain, and others ------ Appellants
Versus
Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Savar Upazila, and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The appellants being plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for a declaration of title and also for a declaration that the suit property cannot be treated as vested and non-resident property (enemy property) alleging, inter-alia, that the Jagat Chandra Karmaker was the C. S. recorded owner of the suit property. After his death his son Gopal Karmaker inherited the said property. This Gopal Karmaker transferred the suit property to one Harendra Lal Saha and Jagannath Saha 71 2 decimals each. After the death of Harendra his property was inherited by his two sons Chandi Gopal Saha and Ashutosh Saha. Jagannath Saha had purchased 7/ 2 decimals of land from Gopal Karmaker. Thereafter, one Parveen Akhter purchased the suit land by the registered deeds of sale from Chandi Gopal Saha and Ashutosh Saha and also from Jagannath Saha. After purchase, this Parveen Akhtar mutated her name in S. A records of right and in Govt. Tahsil Office and paid rents to the Government. From this Parveen Akhtar the present plaintiff-appellants had purchased the suit property by three deeds of sale each measuring 5 decimals. After purchase they also mutated their names in Government Tahsil office and also recorded their names in S. A. khatian.. While the plaintiffs were possessing the suit land, they came to know on 15. 1. 84 that the property in question was declared as vested and non-resident property. This fact has created some cloud over the right title of the plaintiffs and as a result the plaintiffs were compelled to file the present suit. 

 All the issues were taken up together and heard by the learned Subordinate Judge. In this case the plaintiffs examined as many as seven witnesses and the defendant examined one witness only. The plaintiffs filed papers and documentsl6 in number which have been made exhibits No. 1 to 4. The defendant also filed two copies of the lease deed vide Exts. A and A (1), After hearing the parties and perusing the materials evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by the Judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge, the plaintiffs preferred this First Appeal. 

 4. Amjad Hossain is P. W. I. He is also plaintiff No 1. He stated in his deposition that the total area is 15 decimals of land in plot No. 515. He in fact, re-iterated the plaint case stating that the original owner of the suit property was Jagat Chandra Karmaker and his name appeared in the Khatian Jagat Chandra Karmaicer died leavin behind one son, namely, Oval Karmaker. This Copal Karmaker was owning and possessing the suit land and he sold 7/-2 decimals of land to Harendra Saha and 7/2 decimals of land to Jagannath Saha. In this way Harendra Lal and Jagannath became the owners of the suit property and their names had been recorded in the S. A Khatian. Harendra Lal died leaving behind two sons, namely, Chandi Gopal Saha and Ashutosh Saha. These Chandi Gopal Saha and Ashutosh Saha sold their 7 /2 decimals of land to Parveen Akhtar on 29. 7. 81 by a registered sale deed. Jagannath Saha also sold his 7 /2 decimals of land to this Parveen Akhter by a registered sale deed on 7. 8. 81. After purchasing the suit land this Parveen Akhtar recorded her name in the record of rights and mutated her name in the Tahsil Office and while she was owning and possessing the suit land, she sold it to the present plaintiff-appellants by three registered sale deeds dated 2. 1. 85. After purchasing the suit property the plaintiffs have separately mutated their names in the record of rights and also in the Tahsil Office. He further stated that the suit land in question is not an enemy property in view of the facts that this Parveen Akhtar purchased the property from the S. A. recorded owners of the suit property who sold it to the plaintiffs in 1985. He further stated that an inquiry was made in the office of the S.D.O who gave a clearance to the effect that it was not an enemy property. The plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 have been residing in a pucca house on the suit property with their family members. He denied the suggestion that this Harendra Lal Saha another owner long ago left this country for India and this suit property had been treated as enemy property. 

 11. The defendant No. 2 examined one witness named Serajul Karim. This D. W. 1 stated that he is an .Assistant in the office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka. He further stated that one Harendra Lal Saha and hers were the owners of this suit property an all left this country in the year 1965 and Government treated this suit property as vested and nonresident property by Govt. V. P Case No. 45 of 1977. In 1977 one Shafiqul Islam and tWo others were given lease of this property. In 1987 also Bishu Miah and Abdul Jabbar were given lease of the suit property. After taking lease the lessees arc in possession. He stated that he did not know anything about this sale and purchase of the suit property. In cross-examination he stated that on 18. 10. 84 he joined the present post. He could not say the name of mouja, the area of the land and the Khatian number. He did not even see the suit property. He further stated that as the owners of the suit property left for India, the property was treated as vested and non-resident property. But in support of the statement he did not file any Government record before the Court. 

 13.1n the back ground of the aforesaid evidence the learned Advocate Mr. Abu Baker, appearing for the plaintiff-appellants submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge are absolutely illegal in view of the fact that the same are contrary to the evidence on record. He submits that the learned Subordinate. Judge failed to consider the material evidence on record properly and on presumption and hypothesis he treated the suit property as vested and non-resident property, although the defendant failed to produce any document whatsoever claiming the same as vested property. He further submits that in the year 1977 no property of this country can be treated as vested and non-resident property in view of the fact that the law on vested and non-resident property was repealed in the year 1976 vide Ordinance No-92 of 1976. 

 15. The suit property measuring 15 decimals of land is covered by plot No. 515. From the plaint it appears that there was averment to the effect that original C. S. recorded owner was Jagat Chandra Karmaker and after his death it was inherited by his only son Gopal Chandra Karmaker P.W . 1 in his evidence clearly stated that original C. S. recorded owner was Jagat Chandra Karmaker and after his death it was inherited by his son Gopal Chandra Karmaker who sold the suit property to Harendra Lal Saha and two others. In this connection we may refer to the deposition of D.W.1 as well as the written statement filed on behalf of the defendant No.2. In the written statement the defendant No. 2 clearly stated that the suit holding previously belonged to Harendra Lal Saha and others who left this country for India and thereby the suit property became the enemy property, now vested and non-resident property. D. w. 1 stated that one Harendra Math Saha and others were the owners of the suit property. We will see later on whether they had gone to India or lived in this court. But the fact remains that in the written statement this defendant No. 2 himself admitted that the suit property belonged to Harendra Lal Saha and others which clearly shows that the Harendra Lal Saha and others became owners of the suit property and this is supported by the evidence of the P. W. I as well Evidence of D. W. I show that Harendra Lal Saha and others were the owners of the suit property. Above facts show that Harendra Lal Saha and others got right and vide over the suit property from the heirs of Jagat Chandra Karmakar. 

 16, Further, it appears that after purchase this Harendra Lai Saha and Jagannath Saha recorded their names in the S. A. record of rights. Further, P. W. 5 Ashutosh Saha who is the son of late Harendra Kumar Saha stated that he and his brother Chandi Gopal Saha got the suit property by inheritance. P. W. 6 is Chandi Gopal Saha. He also stated that they two brothers inherited 7 /2 decimals of land from their father and they sold the same to Parveen Akhtar. It further appears from the evidence of D. W.1 that Harendra Lal Saha and others were the owners of the suit property. This is a clear admission by the defendant No. 2 that the suit property belonged to Harendra Lal Saha and two others which in fact, supports the case made out by the plaintiffs in the plaint as well as in his evidence. If we consider the averments made in the plaint and the evidence of P.W.1 together with the written statements of defendant No. 2 and the evidence of D. W. 1 it clearly appears to us that Harendra Lal Saha and others became the owners of the suit property and they possessed the same and sold the same to Mrs. Parveen Akhtar by registered sale deeds in 1981. 

 17. Records show that several copies of C. S and S. A Khatians along with several Rent receipts were submitted by the plaintiffs and the same were marked as exhibits. These exhibits were not properly considered by the Court below. In the case of Erfan All Vs. Joynal Abedin Mia, 35 D. L. R. (AD) 216, it was held by our Appellate Division that the Rent receipts are important evidence of possession and the same may be used as collateral evidence of title. Relying upon the above principle settled by the Appellate Division in the above case we hold that the Rent receipts together with the continuous records of right vide exhibits 1 series may be treated as collateral evidence of title in favour of the plaintiffs. Nov, if we consider the oral as well as documentary evidence as stated above, we find that this Harendra Lal Saha and other acquired right and title over the suit property. The documents by which the heirs Harendra Lal and Jagannath transferred the suit land to Parveen Akhtar and the registered document by which Parveen Akhtar transferred the suit land to the present plaintiffs are not disputed at all. So it is held that the learned Subordinate Judge failed to consider the material evidence on record as stated above and he has arrived at a wrong finding stating that there is no evidence to show that Gopal Karmaker transferred the land to Harendra Lal Saha and others. It appears from the Judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge that he did not, in fact, disbelieve the documents as produced by the plaintiffs in the suit. But only because there was absence of any evidence regarding transfer of the suit property from Gopal Karmaker to Harendra Lal Saha and others, he found that in the suit property the plaintiffs did not acquire any right and title. The finding is absolutely incorrect and contrary to the evidence on record and as such it cannot be sustained. 

 20. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the material evidence on record as well as the Judgment of the Trial Court. The findings arrived by the learned Trial Court are contrary to the evidence on record and as such the same cannot be sustained. As a result we hold that the learned Subordinate Judge has illegally passed the judgment dismissing the suit. So, the Judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge are liable to be set aside. 

 22. Send down the L. C records immediately to the Trial Court.

lawyer:
Md Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate with Saidul Alam Khan, Advocate ---- For the Petitioner. 
Sikder Mahmudur Razi, Advocate ----- For the Opposite-Party Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Mohammad Ali ----- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioner 
Vs 
Ali Ahammad and others ----- Defendants-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
4. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner in short is that the suit properties along with other properties were belonged to Jalaluddin, Jorali, Taripullah and Achia Bibi. By an amicable partition the suit plot No. 309 having 56 decimals of land fell in the shaham of Jorali alias Janu, out of 56 decimals he sold 19 decimals of land by the east to the predecessor of the defendants Abdur Rahim and he used to possess the said 19 decimals till his death, Jorali alias Janu while in possession of 39 decimals of land by the west side of the suit plot died leaving only son Kazimuddin and his name was duly recorded in the SA and RS khatian. In the RS Khatian suit land measuring 39 decimals of land was recorded in RS plot No. 435 and was duly published without any objection. Kazimuddin for want of money sold the above said 39 decimals of land to his son Abdul Mojid vide deed No. 2476 on 10-3-1973 and handed over possession on the same date. Thereafter Abdul Majid sold the same to Rahman Ali on 31-12-1976 vide deed No. 7787 and handed over possession to the purchaser. Thereafter Rahman Ali died leaving Asirun Nesa as wife, Mohammad Ali, Idris Ali, Meher Ali, Misir Ali as 4 sons, Hawlatun Nesa, Rashida Begum and Rehena Akhter as 3 daughters who inherited his property. Then Asirun Nesa died leaving the above 4 sons and 3 daughters. The above 4 sons and 3 daughters made an amicable partition of the landed property left by Rahman Ali on 29-10-1998 vide deed No. 10629. In that amicable partition, the plaintiff as 4th party got the suit land in his shaham along with other lands; his brother and sisters got shaham from other land. The plaintiff peacefully possessing the suit land for more than 12 years within the Knowledge of the defendants and others and acquired adverse title by adverse possession. The plaintiff built up house in one portion of the land on 30-3-1998 and planted trees on the rest of the land. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 raised objection that there are mistakes in the deed of Abdul Majid and then the plaintiff having got the original deeds saw that there are mistakes in the deeds which have omitted by the deed writer. Me wrote in the deed Mouza No. 167 instead of 159 plot No. Sabek 399 instead of 309 but the Mai plot No. 435 has been written correctly. Kamizuddin has ownership in plot No. 309 and he had no right to sale the property of plot No. 399. This is a bonafide mistake of the deed writer as well as the parties. The plaintiff sought for declaration of title on the suit land, and further sought for declaration that suit land is not the property of No. 167 Keshrab, of khatian Nos. 229/230 of plot No. 399 rather it is the property of Mouza No. 159 Keshrab, of CS Khatian No. 707 containing CS Plot No. 309 and so on. 

 5. The defendants- Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement; that the said defendants contended that Jalal Uddin, Jorali, Toriqulla and Achia Bibi was the CS recorded owners of the schedule land along with other lands which comprised a total area of 407 decimals of land of 13 plots appertaining to CS Khatian No. 707; that CS record was prepared in their names in equal share; subsequently said Jalal Uddin, Jorali, Toriqulla and Achia Bibi for their convenience divided the schedule land along with their other properties by way of amicable family settlement; by such amicable settlement Achia Bibi got in her saham 38 decimals of schedule plot land along with other properties and the rest 18 decimals of schedule plot land was included in the saham of Jorali; thus the CS recorded owners after amicable settlement was possessing their respective land peacefully to the knowledge of others. Subsequently said Jorali transferred his 18 decimals land of the schedule plot to Abdur Rahim; subsequently Abdur Rahim died leaving behind his sons namely Alauddin, Serajuddin and Mohijuddin who inherited 18 decimals of the schedule plot land along with other properties left by their father; subsequently by way of an amicable settlement out of the said 18 decimals of land 9 decimals of land was included in the saham of Alauddin, 3.5 decimals of land was included in the saham of Serajuddin and 5.5 decimals of land was included in the saham of Mohijuddin. That thereafter Alauddin on 11-10-1955 and Serajuddin on 23-3-1953 sold their portion of land in the schedule plot to Subed Ali, the father of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. On the other hand CS tenant Achia Bibi died leaving behind her only daughter Amirun Bibi and this Amirun Bibi being the owner of 38 decimals land of plot No. 309 along with other land by way of inheritance and sold 38 decimals of land of plot No. 309 and 3 decimals of land of plot No. 358 on 7-4-1960 to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali, that subsequently during SA survey name of Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali was recorded in the SA Khatian correctly; in this way Subed Ali owned and possessed 31.50 decimals of land from CS plot No. 309; subsequently said Subed Ali died leaving behind defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and others as his heirs; that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is possessing the their land peacefully to the knowledge of all; for their convenience they dug some land, filed up some portion and growing trees over the other portion; that during RS survey due to the mistakes of the survey officers less share of land was recorded in the names of their predecessors and the RS record was not prepared correctly; that the defendants are possessing their land by paying rent to the government; that name of CS recorded owner Jorali was never Jorali alias junu; that Jorali did not get in his saham 37 decimals of land from the schedule plot; that Jorali had no son namely Kazimuddin alias Kamizuddin; Kazimuddin alias Kamizuddin never possessed 37 decimals of land from the western portion of the suit plot land; that SA and RS khatian was not prepared in the sole name of Kazimuddin and there was no such scope and if there is any such khatians that would be a collusive and fake one; that Kazimuddin was not the owner of 37 decimals of land and he did not sell the same to his son Abdul Majid on 10-3-1973 and any such deed if so produced that would be a collusive one and ineffective; Abdul Mazid never acquired ownership and possession in the suit land; Abdul Majid did not sell the 37 decimals of land to the father of the plaintiff and he had no right to transfer the said land; that the-plaintiffs had full knowledge about the contents of their alleged deed since 1977; that the plaintiffs has no right, title and possession and their instant suit is a malafide one; therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. On conclusion of the trial, the learned Trial Judge by his Judgment and decree dated 9-6-2004 (decree drawn up and signed on 15-6-2004) dismissed the suit. Learned Trial Judge while dismissing the suit held that admittedly Jorali got 18 decimals of land from Plot No. 309; in paragraph No. 3 of the plaint, the plaintiff claimed that Kazimuddin got 37 decimals of land by inheritance from Jorali but in cross examination as PW 1 he stated that Kazimuddin became the owner by way of purchase and he had not submitted the said document and therefore, PW 1 do not support his case. The learned Trial Judge further held that the defendants claimed that Amirun Nesa became the owner of the land from her mother Achia and DW 1 in his deposition supported the said case. Amirun Nesa sold 38 decimals of land to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali (Ex-Ka) and in the SA Khatian (Ex-2) name of Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali has been recorded. Deed dated 7-4-1960 (Ex-Ka) is a 30 years old document. Therefore, it is proved that Achia got 38 decimals of land in Plot No. 309. Since Kazimuddin has got no right and title in the suit land therefore, the wrong recordings in the deed No. 2476 dated 10-3-1973 is not proved and that statement is not believable. Since Kazimuddin has no right and title therefore, plaintiffs have acquired no right and title in the suit land. The learned Trial judge further held that it is not believable that the predecessors of the plaintiffs did not check the schedule of deed dated 10-3-1973 and 31-12-1973. Plaintiffs did not try to prove that Kazimuddin had no property in the mouza, khatian, plot which has been written in the said deeds. That the plaintiffs failed to prove their exclusive possession in the suit land and the plaintiffs had knowledge about the deeds in question since 1976. Thus the plaintiffs failed to prove their case. Furthermore, while dismissing the suit the learned Trial judge also holds that since the defendants had not taken any steps against RS Khatian No. 231 which has been recorded in the name of Kazimuddin therefore, plaintiff's title over the land in question is not also proved. 

 10. The plaintiff-petitioner having been resentful to the said judgment and decree preferred an appeal before the learned District judge, Narayangonj and the same was registered as Title Appeal No. 240 of 2006; the said appeal was ultimately heard by learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Narayangonj who upon hearing the parties disallowed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 30-11-2010 (decree drawn up and signed on 2-1-2011). While disallowing, the appeal the learned Judge of the Lower Appellate Court held that in the plaint, the plaintiff claimed that Kazimuddin got the land by way of inheritance from Jorali but in cross examination as PW 1 he stated that Kazimuddin became the owner by way of purchase. Therefore, PW 1 does not support his case. Moreover, there is no oral and documentary evidence that Jorali got the entire 56 decimals of land. Regarding alleged wrong writings in the disputed deeds the plaintiffs failed to give any cogent and believable explanation in his cross examination. The plaintiff has got no right and title by dint of exhibit Nos. 6, 7 and 8. The learned Appellate judge further held that Amirun Nesa, daughter of Achia sold 38 decimals of land to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali (Ex-Ka) and in the SA Khatian (Ex-2) name of Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali has been recorded. Therefore, Subed Ali got right and title in the suit land and accordingly defendant Nos. 1 and 2 also acquired ownership in the land. He further held that since PW 2 and 3 are cousins of the plaintiff therefore, their testimony as to possession of the plaintiff is not believable rather the said witnesses admitted the possession of the defendants. PW 3 failed to state the boundary of the land in his cross examination. On the other hand DWs 2-4 gave testimony in support of defendant's possession and they denied plaintiffs possession categorically. The possession of the suit land by the defendants is also evidenced from the fact that they paid rent of the land. While disallowing the appeal the Learned Appellate Judge further reversed the findings of the Trial Court against the defendants on the ground that mere record of rights do not confer any title and extinguish the right of the others and the defendants have successfully proved the title and possession over the suit land. 

 12. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate along with Mr Saidul Alam Khan, Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the impugned judgment and decree are bad in law as well as in fact; that the learned Judge of the courts below failed to consider that RS record in respect of 37 decimals of land was prepared in the name of Kazimuddin; that since the defendants admitted that Joarli had also saham in the suit land therefore, this part admission is regarded to be admission of the entire case of the plaintiff. The learned advocate further submits that since the defendants had not preferred any appeal or cross-objection against the findings of the Trial judge which goes against the defendant therefore, the plaintiffs case should be considered. The learned advocate finally submits that the impugned judgment and decree suffers from non-consideration of materials and evidences on record and prays for making the rule absolute. In support of his submission Mr Nurul Amin, the learned advocate relied on the judgments passed in the following cases: Sheikh Salimuddin vs Ataur Rahman reported in 43 DLR 18, Parul Rani Sen Gupta vs Bangladesh reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 277. 

 13. On the other hand Mr. Sikder Mahmudur Razi, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 opposing the rule, submits that amicable partition amongst the heirs of CS recorded tenants was held after the CS record and the same is also evident from the plaint of the petitioner. He next submits that since the plaintiff-petitioner has not prayed for rectification of the deed in question as per section 31 of the Specific relief Act, therefore the suit itself is not maintainable at all. He next submits that the plaintiff in the original plaint claimed that Kazimuddin became the owner by way of inheritance but (during trial he claimed Kazimuddin became the owner by way purchase and thus gave contradictory statement. Moreover, the identity of Kazimuddin as claimed by the plaintiff is not correct and he is not the son of CS recorded owner Jorali. He further submits that the plaintiff in the original plaint claimed ownership by way of inheritance but by way of an amendment they claimed adverse possession and these two claims cannot run side by side. 

 14. Mr Razi further submits that since the purchase deed of the father of the defendant Nos. 1 & 2 was a properly executed deed which was earlier in point of time and since it is the settled principle of law that kabala deed prevails over the record of rights therefore, the learned Judge of the Appellate court correctly came to the conclusion that the defendants has right, title and possession over the suit land and thereby dismissed the appeal and upheld the decree of the trial court. 

 15. He finally submits that the learned Judge of the Appellate Court being the last court of fact has properly assessed the evidences and materials on record and thereby came to the conclusion that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case and on the other hand the defendants has been successfully proved their title and possession over the suit land and upon such findings dismissed the appeal of the petitioner and upheld the decree of the trial court and most of its findings made in the judgment and therefore, the said judgment does not suffer from any non-reading, misreading, non-consideration of material evidences on record, misconstruction, misapplication of law and fact and therefore, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged. In support of his submission Mr. Razi relied on the judgments passed in the following cases: Guru Charan Mondal vs Sree Bhaba Sindu Sarkar, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 6, Tajul Islam vs Chini Miah, reported in 13 MLR 1, Saeeda Yasmin vs Capital Services Center Ltd, reported in 57 DLR (AD) 189. 

 16. Heard the learned advocates of both the sides, perused the revisional application, the counter affidavit, the impugned judgment and decree as well as the materials and evidence on record. 

 18. It further appears from the cross examination of the PWs 2 and 3 that they virtually admitted the possession of the defendant in the suit land. But it appears from record that the plaintiff did not pray for recovery of possession and from this point of view the instant suit is not maintainable in this present form and nature. 

 21. It further appears from the materials, oral and documentary evidences on record that suit plot No. 309 contains 56 decimals of land and admittedly by way of an amicable settlement Jorali got 18 decimals land in his saham in suit plot No. 309; now, the question remains who got the rest 38 decimals land of the said plot; it is the case of the plaintiff that Jorali got the entire 56 decimals land whereas the claim of the contesting defendant is that the rest 38 decimals land was included in the saham of Achia Bibi; on her death her daughter Amirun Bibi transferred the same to Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali by registered deed dated 7-4-1960 and during SA survey name of said Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali were recorded in SA Khatian No. 627. Exhibit Ka which is the deed dated 7-4-1960 and Exhibit 2 which is the SA Khatian No. 627 supported the defendants' case. Since, after purchase SA khatian was prepared in the name of said Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali it can be said that the said deed was acted upon and said Subed Ali and Nayeb Ali who are predecessors of the defendants, got possession from the date of purchase. 

 22. The contention of the petitioner that since RS record was prepared in the name of Kazimuddin therefore, his case stands docs not deserve any consideration since it is the settled principle of law that kabala deed prevail over record of rights and mere preparation of Khatian in the name of any particular individual without any basis does not confer any title. In the case of Guru Charan Mondal vs Sree Bhaba Sindhu Sarkar, reported in 13 MLR (AD) 6 also supported the same principle. 

 25. This revisional application has been filed against judgment and decree of affirmance. In such a case the petitioner must have to make out a case of misreading, non-reading, misconstruction, non-consideration of the materials and evidences on record which in the instant case the petitioner failed to do. 

 26. It is a settled principle that the findings of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the lower appellate court; which is the final court of fact, is binding on the High Court Division, as a revisional court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case. In the instant case, the learned advocate for the petitioner failed to point out any such exceptional circumstances. Rather from the judgment of the appellate court it is found that in arriving at its findings the said court carefully considered all the material facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, both oral and documentary and consequently these findings of facts are immune from interference in revision.
